Well, that at least rules out a hardware issue. Given your description and given OBS being launched somehow prevents the issue from happening, I'm inclined to say it's something like a driver issue. I mean, if it had been the engine (Godot) itself, OBS being active should not really change anything. There is no link whatsoever between Godot and OBS. Other than... the hardware and the GPU driver.

And if it had been a hardware issue, I'd expect the issue the persist even with OBS running. In fact, I'd expect the problem becoming even more pronounced/severe. So... before trying anything else, I'd suggest doing a complete clean reinstall of the GPU driver. If you're on Windows, use something like DDU ( https://www.guru3d.com/download/display-driver-uninstaller-download/ ) to completely purge the GPU drivers. So there are no traces of it left behind. And then cleanly reinstall the GPU driver.

I'm not sure but I suppose by default it should?!

> I'm not sure but I suppose by default it should?!

It defaults to DX11, as far as I know. You have to explicitly set it to Vulkan. So, given that the fix for your situation was the suggestion to switch to Compatibility in Godot (which uses OpenGL 3.3) and UE5 works fine (while also not using Vulkan), it should be obvious there is _some_ issue with Vulkan on your machine.

On the hardware front, there should not be such an issue though. The 4070 has no trouble dealing with Vulkan, as far as I know. Heck, even my aging 1050 Ti does fine with Vulkan. So, I am going back to my original conclusion -- You have a driver problem. Now, given the fact you did a clean reinstall of it, as per my initial suggestion, the issue most likely is not on your end. My best guess at this time is there some sort of bug crept into the official driver for your GPU.

If you can and if you are willing, try switching to an older version of the GPU driver. To see if that works fine.

I discovered something interesting: Unity also crashed using Vulkan, and when I ran OBS, it became very slow and also crashed my driver. So it seems to be a driver problem, not related to Godot.

> It's a problem with Vulkan;

Primarily, it seems to be an issue with Nvidia's drivers and Vulkan. I've noticed quite a number of people in the issue section here experiencing issues with Godot on Vulkan. All of them on Nvidia GPUs, all of them on Windows. Which is not to shift blame or anything like that. But it just seems to me that there is a very specific combination of pieces here that runs into issues.

- Windows
- Nvidia GPU
- Nvidia driver
- Godot

With those 4 pieces being required to cause issues. Almost as if on some level, the Nvidia driver is handling Vulkan slightly off-spec. In a slightly irregular manner. So, why would running OBS fix it then? Probably just sort of 'anchoring' the Vulkan device. So Godot does not end up losing track of it and crashing as a result.

An internal Godot fix might be to have a more robust handling of a loss of the Vulkan device. So as not to crash to desktop but to close more gracefully at least. Just a thought. I don't know, it's a very weird situation in general. Without a straightforward solution, I feel.

Hi, just want to chime in. I just downloaded Godot today, and couldn't get it to run for more than 5 mins. I came to this thread to find others with the same problem. I was able to solve my problem by changing the Graphics settings in Windows. See screenshot attached.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5110732-b090-4455-970c-287e36dab4c9)
Closing as fixed by driver updates, if this can still be reproduced with up-to-date drivers or anything else is still an issue, please comment here

For anyone else still experiencing this error in 2026 like I did, here are two tips:
1. By default, Godot does not limit the FPS, which can lead to very high GPU load in 3D projects. That was the cause of this exact error in my project (on multiple devices). Limiting the FPS and enabling VSYNC can resolve the issue. 
2. You can export to D3D and add the flag --rendering-driver d3d12 when launching the game.
See also: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html
